chapter: Honors, Gibson and Dorsey late years
title: Growth of Gibson's parties: the Jerome Hotel in Aspen
summary: The second Aspen party outgrew its dining room; Leeman suggested adding the Lawson-Haggart band, and he has kept Gibson's handwritten set lists since 1962.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Those are enough accolades for the present, and now I will get on with some more notes. I'd like to do a fast resume of the Richard Gibson, the Dick Gibson parties that he started in '62 in Aspen. We covered some of that, and the first band which was his favorite -- Condon band, and with Teddy Wilson's trio.

Well, the following year, you know, all his parties have been private subscription -- his guest lists, as they were originally, the party for Mattie Gibson. So the second year, he wanted to elaborate on the party. His guest list, people heard about it, and they heard about it
in Denver, and so many people were asked to be on the list, he kept it down to a minimum. But it was more than he could accommodate in the hotel.
It comes to me now, Milt, because we couldn't recall before -- but the name of the hotel was the Jerome Hotel, and it's a picturesque hotel that goes back to the Gold Rush days.

Now, as I said, the guest list was growing, so how he ever managed -- Dick Gibson talked to management into letting him tear down the partition from the room, the dining room that we were playing in, he tore down the whole wall leading into the lobby of the hotel, so that people could -- he could put more chairs in and the people could be seated properly to see the music.

He asked me the second year -- how can we elaborate and maybe have a few more musicians, because we have a guest list, and it's growing, and I don't want to make any money on this. And I suggested -- he would confide in me quite often, and I suggested the Lawson-Haggard Band whom I had been recording with, it was a great jazz band, according to his likes and tastes and so forth, and so it came to be that second year, he added them to the roster.
And the third year in Aspen, he asked me and Jack Lesberg, and I suggested a bunch of names that possibly he might add, the musicians, so the groups got larger. So he got

a whole bunch of musicians from the coast, and some beautiful people like Eddie Miller and -- well, I shant go into the names because there were so many, as the parties grew, and I have every set -- Richard used to write out the sets of all the musicians who would be following each other on the bandstand, and I have every one from back in '62. I rather think that I'm the only person who has preserved all those things.
